author: Ifmyante
text:
bobyv87 wrote: If, i have four
questions for you regarding TT and managing the trade. I tried to make
them very simple and with short answers. Can you please help me with
these? I try to work on my SLs to keep them as tight as possible and in
that way to increase my R on each trade. Thank you very much!

1. No

2. FTB to any of these can easily bounce price, so stops can be beyond each, managing expectations

3. If there's a clean set of orders very close beyond 5, you can put them beyond that. But this reduces R as well as risk

4. First target is the nearest approach flag. Sine there's a possible range fill between 5 and B, let PA dictate your exit

Yes thanks, at least it lights up the way you see these things and that can makes sense to me.

I still don't explain to myself many stuffs about the RTM material though, both the essence and the way it's presented.

If the best places to look for PA are MPLs, then why not train people to
 find PA in the MPL, with the scale difficulties it implies, rather than
 in the middle of a swing like it's made in part 1?

About the UFL / LFL, why make such a simple example in part 1? The fact
that the example shows a lot of space between UFL / LFL isn't such a
problem to me, but the scale are completely eluded and that's a major
issue when you get to real market. I can understand that scales are a
very complicated topic, but between a full explanation of everything and
 what is in part 1, i guess there could have been a more appropriate
detail level.

Actually i'm not saying anything new here about these lacks because
before the summer 2017 RTM team was speaking about adding lessons about
that amongst other things, so it must have been for some reasons.

The main example of that is the part where it's said that any high or
low can be a target for price and therefore cancel any engulf, there is
almost no mention of scale expect that they can be of "any scale"... How
 to interpret that? There are a hundred ways to interpret it.

And another thing that i can't explain to myself is that in part 1 it's
said we should search engulfs from UFL/LFL, which are presented as
swapping flags (one has to break another), while when you take the
ignored level article, it says that FL can be LS kinks, S/R kinks, break
 into or out of CP kinks. Why not make a coherent definition for
everything and therefore leave no room to incorrect interpretation? Does
 it means that some LS kinks, that aren't a FL, aren't suited for PA?

Same thing about the fact that i just saw some new RTMers doing their
homeworks using the FTR concepts because they somehow still are in the
material. I don't explain myself how these confusions factors still
exist.

author: Ifmyante
text:
i really don't see any reason for confusion, but I'm sorry that you do.

As for the FTR, it's still very valuable, as it can be the first leg of a BSZ, which is eminently tradeable
